name: Eigenvalues
kicker: How much a matrix stretches its special vectors · Named for German “own”
dates: German name used by David Hilbert from 1904
briefing: When a matrix acts on most arrows, it turns them off their lines, but a few special arrows, called eigenvectors, only get stretched, shrunk, or flipped. The number that says how much is the eigenvalue, from the German word _eigen_, meaning “own.” Eigenvalues tell engineers how bridges vibrate and tell physicists which energies an atom can have, and Google’s original PageRank method ranked web pages using the eigenvector whose eigenvalue is 1.
answerHtml: eigenvalues (accept characteristic values, characteristic roots, proper values, or latent roots; prompt on lambda; do not accept “eigenvectors”)

qb.tip: Search QBReader for this answer line (Middle School + Easy High School, power-marked) to see how real tossups clue it.

tossups.p: In 1904, while studying integral equations, David Hilbert began calling these numbers by the German-based name that mathematicians still use. A matrix and its transpose always have exactly the same set of these numbers, which is called the spectrum.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name these numbers λ for which a matrix A times a nonzero vector v equals λ times v.

tossups.p: Mark Kac’s [“KAHT-siz”] 1966 paper “Can One Hear the Shape of a Drum?” asked whether these numbers, which set the frequencies a drumhead can ring at, determine its shape. In 1992, three mathematicians answered no by finding two differently shaped drums that share all of them.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name these numbers that tell how much a matrix stretches its special vectors without turning them.

tossups.p: Every rotation of three-dimensional space has 1 as one of these numbers, because the points on its axis, like the poles of a spinning globe, stay where they are. For a triangular matrix, these numbers are simply the entries on the main diagonal.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name these numbers λ that solve A v equals λ v for a matrix A.

tossups.p: In quantum mechanics, every possible result of measuring a quantity is one of these numbers for a Hermitian [“her-MISH-un”] operator. The time-independent Schrödinger [“SHROH-ding-er”] equation asks for these numbers, which give the allowed energy levels of an atom.
tossups.r: Their name comes from a German word meaning “own.” For 10 points, name these numbers, symbolized lambda, that go with a matrix’s special vectors.

tossups.p: Google’s original PageRank method scored every web page using the special vector that goes with one of these numbers, equal to 1, for a giant matrix built from links. A matrix describing a Markov chain, in which every column adds up to 1, always has 1 as one of these numbers.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name these numbers λ that tell how much a matrix stretches or shrinks a vector without turning it.

tossups.p: The larger of these numbers for the matrix with rows 1, 1 and 1, 0, which produces the Fibonacci numbers, is the golden ratio, about 1.618. For any 2-by-2 matrix, these numbers solve a quadratic equation whose constant term is the determinant and whose middle coefficient is the negative of the trace.
tossups.r: Their name comes from the German word for “own.” For 10 points, name these numbers λ that solve A v equals λ v for a square matrix A.

tossups.p: Reflecting the plane across a line has these numbers 1 and negative 1, because arrows along the mirror line stay put while arrows perpendicular to it flip around. A rotation by 90 degrees has none of these numbers among the real numbers, only i and negative i, because it turns every arrow off its own line.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name these stretch factors λ, each paired with a vector that a matrix only stretches, shrinks, or flips.

tossups.p: Augustin-Louis Cauchy [“koh-SHEE”] coined an older French name for these numbers that survives in the term “characteristic equation.” That equation sets the determinant of A minus lambda times the identity matrix equal to zero, and its solutions are these numbers.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name these numbers, which tell how much a matrix stretches the special vectors it does not turn.

tossups.p: The Cayley–Hamilton theorem says that every square matrix satisfies its own characteristic equation, the equation whose solutions are these numbers. The power method finds the one of these numbers that is largest in size by multiplying a starting vector by the matrix over and over.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name these numbers λ for which a matrix times a nonzero vector v equals λ times v.

tossups.p: Engineers compute these numbers to find the natural frequencies at which a bridge or skyscraper tends to vibrate. Diagonalizing a matrix writes it as P times D times the inverse of P, where the diagonal matrix D holds these numbers along its main diagonal.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name these numbers, whose sum is the trace of a matrix and whose product is its determinant.

tossups.p: In Karl Pearson’s method of principal component analysis, these numbers for a covariance matrix measure how much a set of data spreads out along each main direction. These numbers are the roots of a polynomial found by subtracting lambda from each diagonal entry of a matrix and taking the determinant.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name these numbers λ that say how much a matrix stretches a vector that stays on its own line.

tossups.p: By the fundamental theorem of algebra, every n-by-n matrix has exactly n of these numbers, counting repeats, though some may be complex numbers. Every one of these numbers for the identity matrix, which leaves every vector unchanged, equals 1.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name these numbers λ, from a German word meaning “own,” that solve A v equals λ v.

tossups.p: Similar matrices always share these numbers, and so do a matrix and its transpose, because in each case the characteristic polynomials match. A matrix is singular, meaning it has no inverse, exactly when zero is one of these numbers.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name these numbers λ, each paired with a special vector that a matrix only stretches or shrinks.

tossups.p: The spectral theorem says that every symmetric matrix of real numbers has only real examples of these numbers. The inverse of a matrix has the reciprocals of these numbers, and the square of a matrix has their squares.
tossups.r: Their sum is the trace. For 10 points, name these numbers, symbolized λ, that solve A v equals λ v for a nonzero vector v.

tossups.p: The matrix with rows 2, 1 and 1, 2 has these numbers 3 and 1, since it triples the vector (1, 1) but leaves the vector (1, negative 1) unchanged. The sum of these numbers for any square matrix equals its trace, the total of its main-diagonal entries.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name these numbers that tell how much a matrix stretches the special vectors it does not turn.

clues.t: A number λ for which a square matrix A times some nonzero vector v gives λ times v: A v = λ v
Tells how much a matrix stretches, shrinks, or flips a special vector that stays on its own line
Named from a German word meaning “own” or “characteristic”
Written with the Greek letter lambda (λ); an n × n matrix has n of them, counting repeats
Found by solving the characteristic equation det(A − λI) = 0; they are the roots of the characteristic polynomial
Their sum equals the trace (the total of the main-diagonal entries), and their product equals the determinant
For a triangular or diagonal matrix, they are simply the entries on the main diagonal
A matrix is singular (has no inverse) exactly when 0 is one of them; its inverse has their reciprocals, and its square has their squares
For a 2 × 2 matrix, they solve the quadratic equation λ² − (trace)λ + (determinant) = 0
A reflection has 1 and −1 (arrows on the mirror line stay put; perpendicular ones flip); a 90° rotation has none among the real numbers, only i and −i
Spectral theorem: a symmetric matrix of real numbers has only real ones; the set of all of them is called the spectrum
In quantum mechanics, the Schrödinger equation’s ones are an atom’s allowed energy levels, and every possible measurement result is one of them
David Hilbert began using their German-based name in 1904, while studying integral equations
Augustin-Louis Cauchy coined an older French name for them that survives in the term “characteristic equation”
Every rotation of three-dimensional space has 1 as one of them, because the points on its axis (like the poles of a spinning globe) stay where they are
Mark Kac’s 1966 paper “Can One Hear the Shape of a Drum?” asked if a drum’s frequencies, set by these, fix its shape; in 1992 the answer turned out to be no
For the matrix with rows 1, 1 and 1, 0, which generates the Fibonacci numbers, they are the golden ratio (about 1.618) and about −0.618
Google’s original PageRank scored web pages with the special vector that goes with the value 1 for a giant matrix of links; every Markov chain matrix has 1 as one
A matrix and its transpose have the same ones, and so do similar matrices, because their characteristic polynomials match
Diagonalizing a matrix writes it as P D P⁻¹, where the diagonal matrix D holds them along its main diagonal
Engineers compute them to find the natural frequencies at which bridges and skyscrapers tend to vibrate
The power method finds the one largest in size by multiplying a starting vector by the matrix over and over
Cayley–Hamilton theorem: every square matrix satisfies its own characteristic equation, the equation whose solutions are these numbers
In Karl Pearson’s principal component analysis, the ones for a covariance matrix measure how much data spreads along each main direction
For the identity matrix, which leaves every vector unchanged, every one of them is 1; for a matrix that doubles every vector, every one is 2

trap.title: Value or vector?
trap.body: Every eigenvalue comes with eigenvectors, and the two are separate answer lines: the eigenvalue is the number λ (how much the arrow gets stretched), while the eigenvector is the arrow v itself. A typical answer line says “do not accept eigenvectors.” Clues about the determinant (the product of all the eigenvalues) and the trace (their sum) can also tempt you to name the wrong quantity.
trap.fix: Listen for the noun: “these numbers,” “these scalars,” “λ,” or “how much it is stretched” means eigenvalues; “these vectors” or “this direction” means eigenvectors. If the question wants “this quantity,” a single number for the whole matrix, it may be the determinant or the trace instead.
trap.line: Real answer line: eigenvalues (accept characteristic values, characteristic roots, proper values, or latent roots; prompt on lambda; do not accept “eigenvectors”)
